title: Austin's Park Gift and Market Regulations
summary:
• **Major Land Donation**: Former Governor E.M. Pease gifted 23 acres of land to Austin for use as a public park, located between Ninon Avenue and Shoal Creek—the council accepted the generous donation

• **Market Regulations**: The city banned street vegetable vendors from selling during official market hours to protect merchants who paid for market stalls, with violators facing misdemeanor charges

• **Street Auction Ban**: Auctioneers were prohibited from selling animals, vehicles, or merchandise on city streets (except state-mandated sales) due to noise complaints and pedestrian obstruction at Congress Avenue and Pecan Street

• **Fire Department Funding**: The council approved a $100 monthly salary for a full-time engineer at the Colorado Steam Fire Engine Company No. 2

• **Liquor License Issues**: Four applicants seeking retail liquor licenses were sent back to reapply after failing to meet city ordinance requirements

Communications.
Austin City. May 22, 1875.
To the Mayor & Aldermen of the city of Austin:
Gentlemen - I send you, endorsed a
deed of gift from my wife and myself
to the city of Austin, for twenty three acres of land, lying and situated between Ninson
Avenue and Shoal creek and entirely within the corporate limits of said city, to be used
as a public Park; which, you will perceive by its terms, is to take effect when it shall
have been accepted by a resolution passed by the city Council Mayor and Board of
Aldermen, and entered of record in their
proceedings.
Yours with respect. E. M. Pease

E. M. Pease and lady proper appreciation
of such a valuable donation.
Austin City May 4th 1875
To the Hon. T. B. Wheeler Mayor of the city of Austin
Sir - Pursuant to an appreciation appointment from your honor on the eighth day of
February last, I have made a thorough enumeration of the inhabitants of the city of Austin
up to and including the thirteenth day of April. In making this enumeration I have visited
every house in the city with but few exceptions being able to procure
the names of occupants without going

their houses I have now the honor to
most respectfully submit the following
report to wit: Americans 5157; colored 6497; English of foreign birth 113 Irish foreign
birth 213; Scotch of foreign birth 19; French of foreign birth 65 Germans foreign birth
757 Swedes foreign birth 138; Poles foreign birth 41 Mexicans of foreign birth 297;
Chinese 23; Italians 37; Russians 7; persons sojourning in the city 2700; Total 13,063.
Any additional information I most respectfully refer you to the consolidated Roll now on
file with the city Recorder.
I remain, very respectfully

Robinson & Fridd. Nays: none.
The following Resolution was unanimously
passed, to wit:
Whereas, From and after the first day of May 1875: provisions will be made for the
erection of a vegetable Market House on market Hill. by the renting of stands or stalls
for the shelter and benefit of the gardeners and public, and


 --- Page break --- 

551

Whereas, It being the custom of some market gardners to sell their produce in the
corporate limits during market hours which will result to the detriment and injury to
those paying for stall rights; therefore be it, Resolved by the city Council of the city
of Austin, that no person engaged in the sale of vegetables from any vehicle shall be
allowed to sell or dispose of the same in the corporate limits during market hours, which
shall be until 7 a.m. from the 20th of March to the 20th of September, and until 8 a.m.
from the 20th of September to the 20th of March.
Any violation of this resolution shall be considered a misdemeanor and punished
as in other cases of misdemeanor.
The following resolution was introduced
and read, towit:
Whereas, There being repeated complaints
from pedestrians and citizens doing business in the neighborhood of the crossing of
Congress Avenue and Pecan Street, arising from the excessive noise and shouting from
auctioneers and the daily blocking of the side-walks by a crowd of people attending the
sale of stock by said auctioneers on said streets, thereby impeding and preventing the
free passage of said side-walks; therefore be it. Resolved by the city Council of the city
of Austin, that from and after the passage of this resolution, no animal, vehicle or any
article of merchandise shall be permitted to be hired, or sold at auction in the streets
of this city, except sales in pursuance of the Laws of the State
and a violation of this resolution shall
be a misdemeanor and punished as in
other cases of misdemeanors.
On motion, the yeas and nays were called
and the resolution passed by the following vote, towit: Yeas: Ald. Boardman, Bremond,


 --- Page break --- 

552

Brueggerhoff, Cullen, Dohme, Piper,
Robinson & Todd, Nays- none.
The following resolution was introduced
and read, towit:
Be it resolved by the city Council of the city of Austin, That Colorado Steam Fire Engine
Company No 2, is hereby authorized to elect an engineer to take charge of their engine,
who shall be a competent and skillful engineer and whose duty it shall be to be at all
times on duty at the engine house of said Company; and who shall hold his office, subject
to the regulations of the Fire Department until the her annual election
in said Company. And that said engineer
shall be entitled to a regular monthly salary of one hundred dollars, to be paid by the
city, as other employees are paid.
On motion, the yeas and nays were called and the resolution passed by the following vote;
Yeas, Ald. Boardman, Bremond, Brueggerhoff, Cullen, Dohme, Piper, Robinson & Todd.
Nay, none.
On motion, the following resolution was unanimously adopted, towit: Be it resolved by the
city Council of the city of Austin, That the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to issue

produce directly north and in the rear of the Market House; said building to be in
accordance with the plans and specifications to be found in the Recorders
Office and to be paid out of the income
of said stalls.
On motion, the Council adjourned.
Fred Sterzing
